title: Chapter 43: The Conditions for Survival
content:
Chapter 43:

The Conditions for Survival

He swallowed the words he had been told, crushing them, chewing them over.

It took only a few seconds for them to pass down his throat, settle in his stomach, become flesh and blood, and circulate to his brain. Slowly digesting their meaning, he closed his eyes.

“You’re less shaken than I expected, I suppose. I thought you’d be bawling your eyes out, in fact.”

Perhaps because Subaru’s reaction was surprisingly quiet, Beatrice muttered this in an unexpected tone of voice.

In response to her words, Subaru gave a small nod, “Yeah,” and then,

“I can think of about three possibilities.”

As he spoke, he held up three fingers, showing them to Beatrice standing before him.

As if showing off to the silent girl, he folded down the first of his raised fingers,

“First, this is a black joke, some kind of sick prank. Honestly, can’t laugh at it, but… if someone’s going to pop out with a ‘Prank Successful’ placard, I’m willing to laugh. If it’s coming, now’s the time, you know?”

Despite his request made with one eye closed, Beatrice’s expression didn’t change.

Subaru accepted that the most peaceful possibility had been crushed, and folded his second finger with a sigh.

“Number two, the wounds were too severe. I actually saw my guts spilling out, after all. Even if you tell me I’m just on life support, it doesn’t really click… but I can accept it.”

“There’s no way Bubby and Betty’s treatment would be flawed, in fact. The scars will remain, and even if they aren’t completely fused together yet, they’ll heal back to normal with time, I suppose. We don’t just let someone die when we made it in time, in fact.”

“True. It’s already been proven that you saved me even with my guts hanging out… wait, that was only three or four days ago, wasn’t it?”

It was a bit unclear because of the repeating days, but in the correct timeline, Subaru getting sliced open by Elsa should have been an event from four days ago.

—Just four days after that, he’d fallen into a situation where his stomach was torn open again. A guy dropping his intestines all over the place in such a short time frame might actually be pretty rare.

“Not that I’m happy about it at all… anyway, if that’s the case.”

Waving his remaining third finger back and forth, Subaru brought up the last possibility he could think of.

“There’s only one cause of death that comes to mind.”

Throughout his repeating days at Roswaal Manor, there were several possibilities that had led to Subaru’s death. Among them, the one that matched his current situation was—

“The curse coming back for revenge, huh.”

“It seems a whole bunch were planted on you when you were attacked by the ulgarm pack, in fact.”

As if backing up Subaru’s guess, Beatrice responded thus while crossing her arms.

The white scars left all over his body—the marks of fangs and claws received from multiple ulgarms—Subaru checked them with a look of bitter frustration before saying,

“Just to be sure, is there no way to lift the curses? You’re not just holding out on me, right?”

If he made a wrong move, she had the dangerous tendency to say something like, “I didn’t do it because you didn’t ask me to, in fact,” so he tried prodding at that specific concern.

But she shook her head at Subaru’s question, which was mixed with wishful thinking, and said,

“If it were something that could be lifted, you would be indebted to me beyond all repayment, I suppose.”

“Hey, give me a break. It’s already piled so high it’d be tough to pay it all back.”

He was always just taking and could never give anything back. Not the last time, nor the time before that, nor this time.

Beatrice gave him a questioning look at his nostalgic mutterings, but Subaru brushed it off with a wave of his hand,

“Mind telling me the reason why these curses can’t be lifted?”

“…You may as well know how you’re going to die, in fact. It’s quite simple, I suppose. —There are too many overlapping curses placed on you, and it has become far too complex, in fact.”

“The curses are… overlapping?”

As Subaru tilted his head, unable to picture it, Beatrice spread both of her hands.

Then, to the blinking Subaru, she said,

“Imagine the curses are threads, I suppose.”

As she spoke, a red thread suddenly tied itself between the palms of her hands. Motioning to the taut thread with her eyes, Beatrice tied a knot in it.

“Let’s say this knot is a curse’s spell rite, in fact. In simple terms, lifting the curse would mean untying this knot, I suppose. However,”

Beatrice’s fingers moved deftly, and the number of threads spanning her palms increased. Blue, yellow, green, pink, black, and white threads multiplied one after another. She tied knots in each of them as well, and further tangled the threads together in a complex web—

“If it were just one curse, it could be untangled by tracing it back. But, with multiple threads jumbled up like this…”

Reaching out, Beatrice gestured for him to take the tangled mass of threads. With the threads placed in his extended hand, Subaru stared at the bizarre, intricate pattern and said,

“No matter how you pull or trace it, there’s no way to untangle it… Ah, damn it, this is definitely high difficulty.”

Even if they were to untangle them one by one, there was no telling where to even start.

Of course, given enough time, it probably wasn’t impossible to untangle them.

“You spoke of a half-day limit, right? What was that prediction based on?”

“That is quite simple; in half a day, the ulgarms will get hungry, in fact.”

Beatrice held up a finger, pointing it right at Subaru as she continued.

“The ulgarms’ curse excels at ‘stealing mana from a distant target,’ I suppose. And since a witchbeast’s diet consists mainly of mana… then the reason they cast curses should naturally be easy to imagine, in fact.”

“They attack people because they’re hungry, huh. I see, just as you’d expect from wild animals, it’s simple. I guess I should be thankful they haven’t gotten the munchies until now.”

He wanted to vent his irritation somewhere, but unfortunately, his hands were full of threads. Directing his indescribable emotions at the tight knots, he struggled clumsily to untie them, and Beatrice gave him a puzzled look.

“Aren’t you afraid, I wonder?”

“Huh?”

“This explanation from Betty is a death sentence for you, in fact. Furthermore, Betty and Bubby have the means to save you, yet we won’t do it, using lack of time as our excuse.”

The time Subaru had left was roughly half a day—depending on how empty the beasts’ stomachs were, it wouldn't be strange for it to activate at this very moment.

And in this situation strapped for time, the curses’ spell rites blighting Subaru’s body were likely not so simple that to go challenging it head-on would bear fruit.

That was why Beatrice wouldn’t take the gamble, and the same went for Puck.

While he understood the rationality of their decision, he couldn’t grasp her intention in going out of her way to say it aloud like this.

Beatrice looked straight at Subaru. Toying with the threads in his hands, Subaru suddenly felt like he understood what she was looking for. It was—

“What’s with you—do you want me to blame you?”

“————”

Beatrice fell silent. Choosing silence instead of her usual quick retort, her inner thoughts were impossible to read.

She neither denied nor affirmed it. Subaru gave a wry smile at her attitude and said,

“Your and Puck’s decision is, well, from an emotional standpoint it feels cold, but from a logical one it’s the natural choice. Giving it your all for someone who’s guaranteed to die—it might be beautiful in a story, but it’s only surface-level.”

Pouring all your strength into a life you know is out of reach.

As a way of facing life, it might be beautiful. But looking at it from a realistic perspective, you couldn’t deny the fact that it was a futile effort. Of course, it was precisely because emotions get involved that people sometimes throw themselves into such acts anyway.

“I don’t think you guys are cold. You’re right. —Something else just came to mind that I wanted to ask, is that okay?”

“…What is it, I suppose.”

“Does Emilia-tan know about the curses on me, too?”

The girl who was still sleeping in the room Subaru had been resting in, exhausted from nursing him.

How had she faced a situation that Puck and Beatrice had already given up on? That alone worried him endlessly.

Beatrice shook her head at Subaru’s question,

“That mixed-blood girl doesn’t know, in fact. The reason Bubby isn’t touching your curses is to keep her from finding out they exist, in fact.”

“…Ah, I see. Puck can’t leave Emilia-tan’s side even while lifting curses, and if he did, it’d inevitably be obvious that I’m cursed and that breaking it is a long way off.”

If they kept quiet until the curses activated, she would only have to suffer a psychological scar once. If Puck was prioritizing Emilia above all else and had decided the tragedy was unavoidable, it was an understandable way of thinking.

Reading into the intentions of Puck, who was shrewder than his appearance suggested, Subaru then said,

“So, then.”

Signaling a shift in the conversation, Subaru pointed a finger at Beatrice. Watching her brow furrow slightly at the gesture, he continued,

“I figure you’re not mean enough to come all the way here just to give me a death sentence, though?”

“…Just what do you think you know about Betty, I suppose.”

“At the very least, it feels like we’ve known each other four times longer than you think we have.”

Looking at the girl whose frown and suspicions were deepening, Subaru thought back on the long yet short two-odd weeks he had rushed through.

His relationship with Ram and Rem was better than it had been since the first loop. His bond with Emilia was good, ignoring how much bawling his eyes out while resting on her lap might have affected her opinion of him. He had uncovered the identity of the curse arts user who kept tormenting him, and he had even managed to save the lives of the village children.

Looking back on these repeating loops, his score this time was close to perfect.

If only his own crucial life had been factored into the equation.

“When I was getting chewed up head to toe by those dogs, I honestly thought I was dead. How pathetic.”

The sensation of his life slipping away that he had experienced time and time again—Subaru had yielded to it.

He had grown too used to death. He’d developed a habit of giving up. Even after coming this far, even after doing all this.

More than anything,

“You, Rem, and Emilia-tan treated my wounds, right? If you were planning on abandoning me over some curses, you wouldn’t have patched me up this well.”

It was an insult to the girls who had desperately kept him alive, even when he had selfishly given up on his own life.

Including the small cat who had used his short limbs to stitch Subaru’s body back together with thread.

“You guys are way too bad at lying.”

“…It’s a fact that the chances of saving you are incredibly low, in fact. And that Bubby is trying to keep that girl from getting involved with the method.”

“Playing the bad guy to take the brunt of my anger over that is way too considerate for a little girl. —Let me hear it, then. This microscopic possibility.”

Forming a tiny circle with his thumb and index finger, he showed it to Beatrice, inviting her answer.

After a brief hesitation, she let out a resigned sigh.

“Since it was the ulgarms that cursed you, the nature of it must undoubtedly be to drain your mana by the roots, in fact.”

He understood that. And Subaru had already experienced its potency firsthand.

Therefore, the moment the ulgarms that cursed him decided to start their “meal,” Subaru’s fate would be sealed. After all, once a curse activated, there was no way to prevent—

“Wait. Then how were the kids’ curses lifted?”

The children they found deep in the forest had been severely weakened. Their condition should have been almost identical to the curse Subaru had received. His thoughts hadn’t reached that far at the time, but—

“If the curses had activated and the kids were having their mana drained, the pattern should be that they get sucked dry until they’re empty. Yet, those kids are safe—you’re not gonna tell me that was another lie to make me feel better, right?”

If so, that was something even Subaru couldn’t bring himself to forgive.

But Beatrice stopped Subaru’s hasty assumptions by holding out her hand,

“You’re too hasty. You should listen until the end, in fact. But you are close to the core of it, I suppose. —We were able to lift the village children’s curses. That method happens to match the faint possibility that might save your life, in fact.”

“The difference between the kids… and me?”

Subaru’s thoughts raced at Beatrice’s explanation.

The difference between his curses and the children’s. Their curses were single, while his were multiple. Activated curses. Unactivated curses. Curses that steal mana. Weakening from stolen mana. Stolen mana. Stolen mana becoming a witchbeast’s meal. —If that was the case…

A single possibility flashed through his mind like lightning, and Subaru raised his head, turning back to Beatrice.

“If the caster dies, where does the stolen mana end up?”

Beatrice’s expression remained unchanged at the question; she merely gave a single nod.

“If it has nowhere to go, the curse loses its effectiveness entirely. This is only on the condition that this curse’s spell rite is designed not to kill the target, but to steal their mana, in fact.”

With Beatrice’s confirmation, Subaru found his internal conviction.

The children’s curses—their progression had stopped because the witchbeast that originally cast them died. And if the caster died, what remained in the children’s bodies was merely the spell rite, which was easy for Puck and Beatrice to undo.

The number of witchbeasts that lost their lives in that forest last night must have been quite high.

Starting with the one Subaru took down in their first encounter, a considerable number had been slaughtered by Rem’s hands during their escape.

Assuming the witchbeasts that cursed the children were among them, there was currently no evidence to disprove his theory.

And that certainty simultaneously meant—

“Ah, I see. So that’s how it is.”

Acknowledging that his reasoning was now rock solid, Subaru realized it.

The meaning behind why Beatrice continued to stand before him with an attitude bordering on sorrowful.

Given that it was impossible to lift his curses the normal way, there was no other method to break the curses placed on Subaru but to kill the casters.

However,

“There are way too many of those things that cursed me to narrow it down.”

Turning around, Subaru looked toward the forest where the witchbeasts resided.

Surrounded by a barrier, the village and the forest were separated by something non-physical. Deep within the depths of that forest was the witchbeast pack, which had likely scattered.

Seeking them out and exterminating them within half a day was impossible.

“Ah, dammit…”

Almost bursting into laughter despite himself, Subaru pressed a hand to his forehead and looked down.

It all made sense now. He was staring directly at a reality he couldn’t turn away from.

Unless the ulgarms were wiped out completely, Subaru’s life couldn’t be saved.

The sheer difficulty of pulling that off in under half a day. Above all, the danger of setting foot in that forest and facing down a pack of witchbeasts—these were the things that made Puck hesitate and served as the reason he refused to inform Emilia of the truth.

“Bubby is…”

“You don’t have to say it, I know. If Emilia-tan found out, knowing her, she’d definitely push herself too hard. That makes me incredibly happy, but… it’s incredibly terrifying.”

She was the kind of person who would unhesitatingly suffer a loss for the sake of others, so even seeing the possibility that she could pull it off, Subaru could never ask it of her.

Because if, by some million-to-one chance, he lost her before his eyes, Subaru was certain to experience an agony so great that having his own body torn apart a hundred times over wouldn’t even compare.

“The difficulty level is goddamn demonically possessed. There’s just no way, it’s impossible. I give u—”

“Is that why you are giving up?”

As Subaru started to say it, that voice revived in his mind.

Mixed with static, it was distant, a thin voice that seemed to echo from the bottom of his subconscious.

With a gasp, he raised his head and looked around.

Aside from Subaru and Beatrice, there was no one else here. And yet, that voice just now—

“Is there any other way to save him?”

A clinging, pleading voice. Yet somewhere within it hid a tragic resolve.

“Did your head start hurting, I suppose? I wouldn’t blame you, in fact.”

“That is all, I suppose. The rest is up to you, in fact.”

Over the voice of the Beatrice in front of him overlapped different words from the same Beatrice.

He didn’t know where. But a conversation he had definitely heard somewhere flashed back to him.

His vision flickered, and clutching his head amidst the pounding headache and blaring alarm bells, Subaru almost dropped to his knees, panting heavily.

“—m will definitely save you.”

At that echoing voice of determination and resolve, he forced his buckling knees to stand firm.

The voice that said it—he recognized the voice making that vow.

And he realized. The thing he needed to ask.

“—Where’s Rem?”

Since this morning, Subaru hadn’t caught a single glimpse of the blue-haired girl.

They were supposed to have returned from the forest together. After all, it must have been her who carried the heavily injured Subaru and the children back. Puck had stated as much, too.

However, that was only up to the point of their return.

Were her injuries so severe that she was still resting somewhere?

—He didn’t know if it was due to her Demonification or what, but they said she had no external wounds.

Then was she going around the village with Ram, working hard to take care of the villagers?

—If Rem could get into the kitchen, Ram’s “specialty” steamed potatoes never would have been served.

Then, where was she right now, when she wasn’t injured but hadn’t even entered the kitchen?

“Beako… Beatrice, where is Rem?”

At Subaru’s faltering question, Beatrice stroked one of her drill-curls,

“If you were in the same position, what would you do, I suppose?”

“That’s not an answer!”

Frustrated by her evasive phrasing, Subaru stepped forward to snap at her. However, perhaps as a backlash from moving so abruptly, his blood-deprived body tilted sharply, thwarting his advance.

Stumbling, Subaru staggered in place.

He knew he was just lashing out. And he understood that Beatrice was acting this way precisely to take it for him.

Even knowing her consideration, he couldn’t help but be infuriated by his own baseness in trying to lean completely on her kindness.

Right then,

“—Ah, you’re both here. Sorry, but do you know where Rem is?”

Had she heard his angry shout? The pink-haired girl ended up making an appearance from a corner of the plaza. She gave the two of them a puzzled look as they faced each other, then tilted her head to prompt them about her question.

Toward her gesture, Beatrice maintained her familiar, indifferent expression.

But Subaru couldn’t pull off that kind of poker face. Unable to look at the older sister who was the spitting image of the girl in his mind, he reflexively looked away.

Subaru’s blatant reaction, and the place where the two of them were talking.

Connecting some sort of dot between those things, Ram suddenly clouded her expression, muttering, “No way,”

“—Clairvoyance, awaken.”

Slipping a hand into her hair, Ram covered one of her eyes as she murmured this.

Immediately after, witnessing the transformation that occurred in her, Subaru let out a groan of shock.

Covering her left eye, the expression with her right eye wide open became thickly traced with bulging veins. The sight of blue-green veins popping on her pale face was grotesque, and the state of Ram’s right eye—which looked less bloodshot and more like a literal pool of blood—only spurred on the gruesomeness.

Disregarding Subaru’s astonishment, Ram, having undergone this transformation, made her lips tremble,

“—Ram can’t see her. No way, Rem, you couldn’t have gone beyond the barrier?!”

With her eyes still bloodshot, she turned around, her feet heading straight for the forest where the barrier had been recast.

Without thinking, Subaru grabbed her shoulder,

“Wait, you know where she is?!”

“As long as Ram can get inside the barrier… don’t stop Ram, Barusu!”

Ram tried fiercely to shake off Subaru’s hand on her shoulder. But Subaru was equally desperate not to be peeled away. Restraining her movements, he looked back and yelled,

“Beatrice!”

“—I presented a possibility, that is all, in fact. Setting aside Bubby, who doesn’t want to expose that mixed-blood girl to danger, Betty is also out of the fight being this far from the Forbidden Library, I suppose. And even if you went yourself, you’d be of absolutely no use. The options were limited, in fact.”

“That’s not what this is about… Then, Rem really did—”

—She went into the witchbeast-infested forest, all by herself, intending to wipe out the pack.

If one were to list the people who counted as fighting strength in this situation, then it might indeed be the correct decision. In fact, Rem’s power had overwhelmed the witchbeasts in the night forest.

However,

“How many of those things can use magic? To begin with, how is she supposed to know when my curses have been lifted? Just killing and killing them one by one, that goes way past just striking blindly!”

“What do you mean? Barusu’s curses were supposed to have been lifted…”

At Subaru’s blood-curdling shout, Ram also clouded her bloodshot eyes. Then turning to Beatrice, Ram rushed to her side,

“What is the meaning of this, Lady Beatrice? What exactly is Rem—?!”

“In order to break the complexly tangled curses of the witchbeasts, she went into the forest to annihilate the ulgarm pack serving as the casters, in fact. —A method offering a possibility of saving both that human over there and your sister, I suppose. However, the odds are infinitesimally small.”

At Beatrice’s blunt words, Ram was momentarily at a loss for words.

But quickly shifting her expression from grief to resolve, she immediately broke into a sprint to chase after her sister and dive into the forest without hesitation.

“—Wait!”

Throwing himself directly in front of her with his arms spread wide, Subaru blocked Ram’s path. The pink-haired girl shot a sharp, piercing glare at his stance,

“Move, Barusu. Ram doesn’t have the leeway to be gentle right now.”

“I’m not telling you not to go without a plan! I just have a few things I need to ask you, so answer them, honestly.”

“Ram doesn’t have time for…”

“If you want to save Rem, and if you consider me even a little bit of an ally, then listen to me. I want to raise our chances, even by just a little bit.”

Hearing that it was a way to help her sister Rem, who was likely in a life-or-death predicament at this very moment, Ram’s stubborn stance wavered slightly.

Seeing her forward momentum loosen, Subaru pressed his advantage,

“I only have two questions. First, with your Clairvoyance power, can you locate Rem inside the forest?”

“…Yes, Ram can. Ram’s clairvoyance lets her eye share the visions of any ‘beings on Ram’s same wavelength’ within range, so if she shifts through the incoming sights one after another, she’ll definitely reach her.”

“So rather than your eye seeing through things, it surveys the scene from multiple fields of vision. I can’t quite picture what that looks like… but, if it means we can regroup with Rem, that’s perfect.”

Nodding at clearing the first condition, Subaru then held up a second finger,

“Then, number two. —Ram, are you the type of maid who can fight?”

“In what sense are you asking that?”

To Ram, who narrowed her eyes and shot the question back, Subaru prefaced with a “Well, you know,” and said,

“Before we regroup with Rem, there’s no telling where we’re gonna clash with the witchbeasts. If you can’t defend yourself, forget about it. Just so you know, if it comes to a fight, I’ll totally be dragging you down.”

“W-Wait a minute. Were you planning on coming with me, Barusu?”

At Subaru, who spoke of his lack of skill with utmost confidence, Ram used a rare, flustered tone. Nodding in understanding of her exasperation, he replied,

“I get why you’re shaken, but it’s a necessary condition, you know? Well, honestly, if our only goal is Rem coming back alive, you could say you don’t really need me, but…”

The second half of his sentence trailed off, and Ram gave him a suspicious look, seemingly unable to hear it.

Seeing her expression, Subaru hastily waved both hands,

“Now that it’s come to this, we want all of us to break through the fifth day don't we! Only when we pull that off will it have been worth trying over and over again like this. So please, let me ask this favor of you.”

Ram’s lips trembled as if unsure what to say to Subaru, who was pressing his hands together in a prayerful plea.

However, in the end, she let out a sigh, swallowing all those words back down.

“—If you’re expecting Ram to fight as well as an Oni-transformed Rem, it’s impossible.”

“Meaning?”

“Unlike Rem, Ram is ‘hornless,’ so she cannot undergo a complete Oni transformation. Unlike Rem, Ram is not proficient in hand-to-hand combat either; Ram can just use slightly extreme wind-type magic.”

Answering so, Ram lightly flicked her finger, and a strong gust of wind shook Subaru’s hair.

If the spell that had just interfered with nature were to become more vicious, it would probably turn into something with the power to gouge out Subaru’s right leg or neck. Thinking about that made even this gentle breeze send shivers down his spine.

However, if he were counting on it as an ally’s fighting strength, there was nothing more reliable.

“Beatrice! I’m going into the forest with Ram now. If Emilia-tan wakes up before we get back, just make up some excuse for us.”

“…Bringing that blue-haired girl back means giving up on your own life, in fact. Do you truly understand that, I suppose?”

“That’s a bit off. Let me correct you.”

To Beatrice, who questioned his resolve in a low voice, Subaru waved his finger side to side, going “Tsk, tsk, tsk,”

“Getting used to death and making a habit of giving up is just stupid. Life is precious, you only get one. I was able to figure that out because you guys gave it your all to tie me to it. So, I’m going to put up a pathetic, ugly struggle.”

After he had once selfishly given up on his life, they had tied it back together for him.

That was why Subaru being as he was now, the pulse of life ticking away within him, was the result of the many people reaching out their hands to him.

Because this was overtime granted to him by them going to such lengths,

“Let’s stage a comeback. I bounced back to this point from such a terrible state. Being the greedy guy I am, I can’t help but want to see an epilogue that includes me.”

Ridiculous logic and an entirely improper explanation.

He gave an answer that didn’t conform in the slightest to what Beatrice had intended, yet Subaru puffed out his chest with the most triumphant, smug look imaginable.

“What you’re thinking is beyond me, in fact. But do as you please, I suppose. The options have been presented. From there, what you choose is up to you, in fact.”

“So that’s how you sent Rem off, too. Well, thanks, Beako.”

Looking back at the forest, he thought of the girl who must still be fighting within its deep darkness.

—That meddling, jump-to-conclusions idiot. Always selfishly imagining how others feel, selfishly jumping to conclusions, and acting entirely on her own. You’ve gotta be kidding me.

“Just as much as you're thinking about wanting to do something for me, I also want to do something for you, dammit!”

Cracking his knuckles to back up his resolve, he declared toward the witchbeasts’ forest.

To the pack of black beasts dwelling in its depths, and to the supernatural entity that dragged Subaru into this fate—a declaration of war that he had made once before and had almost forgotten.

“Come on, let’s go for one last big gamble. —Bring it on, oh inevitable fate!”

Stage 2, “Roswaal Manor,” Day 4: The fifth attempt began—.
